# Pickup classifier: results (generated by `python -m classifier.train`)

> **Synthetic data only** until real Redmi 14C sessions are recorded (see MODEL_CARD.md). These numbers validate the pipeline and the physics model; they are **not** a measurement of real-world accuracy.

Windows (all triggered by the production MotionTrigger): train 10000, validation 4000, IID test 4000, shift test 4000. Label mix: 50% pickup, 25% bump, 12.5% slide, 12.5% set-down.

The shift test uses surfaces (glass table, sofa), phone masses (<0.17 kg, >0.24 kg) and sensor profiles (40 Hz or 100 Hz delivery, 0.02-0.06 m/s^2 noise, 19-77 mm/s^2 quantization, 2-4 g range, larger bias and jitter) that never appear in training.

## Selected model: `logistic`

Verdict PICKUP iff the calibrated logit >= **0.000** (P(pickup) >= 0.5001). Rule applied: midpoint of the validation gap; validation gap between the 0.5% lowest pickups and the 0.5% highest non-pickups = 3.60 logits. Platt calibration a = 0.8393, b = 0.2889.

## Calibration (`logistic`, IID test)

ECE 0.0017, Brier 0.0009, log loss 0.0040. P(pickup) is calibrated to this 50/50 synthetic mix; on the phone most motion windows at night are not pickups, so the prior-free threshold is what matters.

## Trigger coverage (simulated events that produced a window)

The classifier only sees motions that fire the MotionTrigger (|a| off rest by 1.2 m/s^2, or gravity 12 deg off). Gentle events below that never reach it; for pickups the FaceDownDetector (tilt > 40 deg) and the hard screen-on / unlock breaks still apply.
